title: ARTIFICIAL SINGULARITY
summary: Long exposure light dynamics experiment conducted during camera familiarization and astrophotography preparation activities.
process: This field experiment was conducted as part of camera familiarization and long exposure photography training before operational astrophotography missions.
Steel wool was ignited and rotated in controlled circular motion while long exposure images were captured using manual settings.
The experiment also served as a practical demonstration of Newtonian mechanics and ballistic trajectories.
conclusion: The experiment successfully produced an artificial singularity-like visual effect using long exposure photography.
The session provided valuable practical experience in exposure control, motion capture and image post-processing.
The resulting trajectories visually demonstrate several aspects of Newton's laws of motion.
notes: This experiment involved real fire and hot metal particles. Appropriate safety precautions are essential. Final images were post-processed using Adobe Photoshop.
